sourceTitle: Our software engineering interviews are changing a little
postText:
Why your next dev hire interview should feel like a design sprint

- Traditional coding whiteboards are losing relevance; candidates now expect real-world context.
Instead of abstract puzzles, I now start with a snippet from our production codebase.

- Pair-programming a live micro-service on a shared repo reveals problem-solving speed and collaboration habits better than a timed algorithm.
It also surfaces how they handle version control conventions and error handling under pressure.

- Including a brief architecture discussion-ask them to sketch a scalable AWS solution for a simple API-shows cloud-mindset and trade-off thinking.
The exercise uncovers their awareness of cost-optimisation, security groups, and CI/CD pipelines-critical for modern cloud teams.

- Giving feedback instantly, even if the candidate doesn’t get the role, builds brand goodwill and provides data for future interview tweaks.
Candidates appreciate the transparency, and the data helps us refine difficulty levels for future rounds.

- Adding a short ‘culture fit’ scenario-like how they'd handle a production outage-reveals communication style and ownership mindset.
I’ve seen this predict on-call performance better than any resume bullet.

What interview tweak has given you the clearest signal of a candidate’s fit?
